title: Alchemy Lab
seoTitle: Alchemy Lab – Mix Elements, Discover 692 Things
description: Play Alchemy Lab free: mix water, fire, earth and air to discover 692 elements, from steam and volcanoes to unicorns, rockets and pizza.
controls: Tap an element in your list
Put it on the table, picked and ready to mix
Mix it with the picked one
Double tap an element on the table
Drag an element off the table
Pick and mix with the keyboard
Take the focused element off the table
lede: Alchemy Lab is a free element mixing game on a magic workbench. You begin with water, fire, earth and air. Mix any two and see what happens: steam, mud, lava, a volcano, then life, animals, cities, rockets and birthday cakes. There are 692 elements to find, every one with its own emoji, and the only way to find them is to experiment.

p: Your elements are listed under the table on a phone and beside it on a bigger screen. Put two of them together and, if they belong together, they turn into something new. A new discovery glows gold, gets a bell-like chime and joins your list with a pink dot, so you can always spot your latest finds.

If two elements do not combine, both simply wiggle and stay where they are, so there is nothing to lose by trying. The counter at the top shows how many of the 692 elements you have found. There is no timer and no way to fail: play for five minutes or come back to the same lab for weeks.
Every element in the lab grows from the four you start with. These ten are made straight from them. Everything after that is up to you.

ol: Mix every new element with water, fire, earth and air first. Between them, the four basics appear in 154 recipes, and fire and water are two of the busiest elements in the whole book.
Try an element with a copy of itself. Two of the same often make something bigger: two bricks make a wall, two walls a house and two houses a village.
Think about what happens in real life. Heat changes things, cold freezes them, water washes and wind wears things down. Time is an element too, and it makes plants grow into trees.
Life is the key to the animal kingdom. Once you have it, mix it with places such as the ocean, the forest or a patch of dust.
When you make a human, try it with everything. People are part of more recipes than any other element, from cooks and farmers to astronauts.
Use the search box when your list gets long. Typing just a few letters is enough.
Stuck? Press Hint. It names one of your elements that is part of a recipe you can make right now, and shows the emoji of the thing it will make.

p: Some discoveries are the end of their line: a unicorn, a pizza or a black hole does not mix into anything else. These final elements have a gold edge in your list, so you do not waste time trying them. Collect them all the same, because they count towards your total.

Your discoveries and the elements on your table are saved in this browser on this device, so you can close the page and carry on later. The round arrow button at the top starts a new game with just the four basics, after asking you first.

sections.h: Where the four elements come from
p: The idea that the world is made of earth, water, air and fire is about 2,500 years old. The Greek thinker Empedocles, who lived in Sicily in the fifth century BC, described them as four roots that are mixed together by Love and pulled apart by Strife. Plato later called them elements and matched each one to a regular solid: the cube for earth, the pyramid-shaped tetrahedron for fire, the octahedron for air and the icosahedron for water.

Aristotle gave each element two of four qualities: fire is hot and dry, air hot and wet, water cold and wet, and earth cold and dry. Change one quality and one element could, in theory, turn into another. That promise of transformation is what drove the alchemists of the Middle Ages and the Renaissance, who tried to turn ordinary metals into gold.

Modern chemistry grew out of their workshops. In 1661 Robert Boyle questioned the four elements in his book The Sceptical Chymist, and in 1789 Antoine Lavoisier published a list of 33 simple substances. Chemists now know 118 elements, but the four classical ones live on in games like this one.

sections.h: The alchemists' signs on the table
p: Look closely at the chalk drawing on the lab table. The four small triangles around its edge are the signs alchemists used for the elements: a triangle pointing up for fire, pointing down for water, and the same two with a line across them for air and earth. Inside them sits a circle around a square around a triangle around a smaller circle, a figure that 17th-century alchemy books used for the philosopher's stone, the legendary substance that was meant to turn metals into gold.

A few recipes are a nod to the same tradition. Alchemists linked each metal to a heavenly body, with gold belonging to the Sun and silver to the Moon, so in this lab metal and the Sun make gold, and metal and the Moon make silver. The flask on the game's icon is an alembic, the glass still alchemists used to distil liquids.

faq: 692 in total: the four you start with and 688 to discover. 68 of them are final elements that do not combine any further.
Does the order of the two elements matter?
No. Water with fire and fire with water both make steam. Every recipe works in either order.
Can I mix an element with itself?
Yes. Tap it twice in your list, or double tap it on the table to make a copy and then put the two together.
Are the recipes always the same?
Yes. Every recipe in the lab was written by hand, so the same two elements always give the same result, on any device.
Why does an element look different on my computer?

Each element uses a standard emoji, and some of the newer ones are missing on older systems such as Windows 10. When that happens the game shows a similar older emoji instead, so you never see an empty box.
Is Alchemy Lab good for children?
Yes. There is no timer, nothing to lose and nothing scary, and reading the names of new discoveries is part of the fun.
